variants.title: Build a RAFT record
variants.context: RAFT records are built from the production retrieval path: freeze the retrieval profile, write answerable questions with split isolation, label every oracle passage, sample distractors the retriever actually returns, and version the complete record.
variants.prompt: A team starts building training records for a bounded support domain. Put the construction steps in order.

items.text: Version the complete record: question, passage IDs, oracle presence, target, retrieval profile, and reviewer identity.
Label every passage required to support the answer and verify the target against the source.
Sample distractors from the confusing passages this retriever returns, not from random text.
Create answerable questions from real intents, split by source or topic so near duplicates do not leak.
Freeze the retrieval profile: corpus snapshot, chunker, metadata filters, embedding model, reranker, and top-k.

variants.hint: What has to be fixed before any passage can be sampled?
variants.explanation: The retrieval profile comes first because every later step describes passages that only exist relative to that profile.

variants.title: Build a RAFT record
variants.context: RAFT records are built from the production retrieval path: freeze the retrieval profile, write answerable questions with split isolation, label every oracle passage, sample distractors the retriever actually returns, and version the complete record.
variants.prompt: The corpus is a policy handbook whose clauses overlap heavily, so plausible near neighbors are everywhere. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Pull the hard distractors from the near-neighbor clauses the retriever returns for those questions.
Write questions from real user intents and split them by source so overlapping clauses stay on one side.
Store the record with passage IDs, oracle presence, the retrieval profile, and the reviewer who approved it.
Record the corpus snapshot, chunker, filters, embedding model, reranker, and top-k that production uses.
Label each clause that is genuinely required to support the answer and verify the target text against it.

variants.hint: Which step decides whether the model practices real evidence selection?
variants.explanation: Hard distractors have to come from the production retrieval distribution, otherwise the model learns to dismiss text it will never see.

variants.title: Build a RAFT record
variants.context: RAFT records are built from the production retrieval path: freeze the retrieval profile, write answerable questions with split isolation, label every oracle passage, sample distractors the retriever actually returns, and version the complete record.
variants.prompt: A new chunker and reranker shipped, so the retrieval distribution changed. Put the rebuild steps in order.

items.text: Keep the existing questions but re-run them through the changed retrieval path.
Re-label oracle passages against the new chunk boundaries before trusting any old label.
Version the rebuilt records so the old and new mixtures are never reported as one dataset.
Resample distractors from the new retriever's output instead of reusing the previous ones.
Re-freeze the retrieval profile against the new chunker, reranker, and top-k.

variants.hint: Old labels describe chunks that may no longer exist.
variants.explanation: Rebuild records when the retrieval distribution changes materially, and version them so results stay comparable.

variants.title: Keep the system boundary
variants.context: RAFT fine-tunes only the generator. The request still flows from a normalized question through the independently versioned retriever to the fine-tuned generator, and evidence checks still gate what is served.
variants.prompt: A fine-tuned generator is live and a normal question arrives. Put the request path in order.

items.text: Let the RAFT generator select the relevant passages, resist distractors, and produce the trained answer format.
Search the deployed corpus with the versioned retriever, its declared filters, reranker, and top-k.
Run evidence checks on citations, unsupported claims, policy boundaries, latency, and fallback behavior.
Normalize the user question without changing its information need.

variants.hint: Which stage was fine-tuned, and which stays independently versioned?
variants.explanation: RAFT changes one component. Retrieval and the evidence checks around it remain separate, versioned parts of the system.

variants.title: Keep the system boundary
variants.context: RAFT fine-tunes only the generator. The request still flows from a normalized question through the independently versioned retriever to the fine-tuned generator, and evidence checks still gate what is served.
variants.prompt: A user asks something the corpus does not answer, and retrieval returns only distractors. Put the path in order, ending with what is served.

items.text: Evidence checks confirm the response carries no unsupported claim before it reaches the user.
Normalize the question without inventing a narrower information need.
The generator applies the product's missing-evidence contract instead of answering from a distractor.
The versioned retriever searches the corpus and returns passages that support nothing.

variants.hint: The contract for missing evidence is a product decision, not a model reflex.
variants.explanation: Missing-evidence behavior belongs to the declared answer, defer, or abstain contract, and the evidence checks still gate the response.

variants.title: Keep the system boundary
variants.context: RAFT fine-tunes only the generator. The request still flows from a normalized question through the independently versioned retriever to the fine-tuned generator, and evidence checks still gate what is served.
variants.prompt: A source document is updated in the deployed corpus. Put the events in order for the next matching question.

items.text: The retriever returns the updated passage for the next matching question.
Evidence checks validate the citation against the passage that was actually retrieved.
The generator answers from that retrieved passage rather than from memorized text.
The new document version enters the deployed corpus and its index snapshot.

variants.hint: Which part of the system carries current facts?
variants.explanation: Facts stay refreshable because they live in the corpus; fine-tuning taught evidence use, not the content itself.

variants.title: Count what the model practices
variants.context: The P fraction sets how many training questions keep an oracle in their context, and the context size sets how many passage slots each record holds. These counts are exact for a recipe; they predict what the model practices, not how well it will do.
variants.prompt: A run uses 12,000 questions and keeps an oracle in the context of 70 percent of them. How many records train with no oracle in their context?
variants.hint: The P fraction splits the record count, nothing else.
variants.explanation: The remaining share keeps the answer target while removing the oracle, so it is the part of the run that presses on domain knowledge rather than evidence selection.

mistakes.feedback: That is the oracle-present share; the question asks for the remaining records.
That applies 10 percent instead of the 30 percent with no oracle.

variants.title: Count what the model practices
variants.context: The P fraction sets how many training questions keep an oracle in their context, and the context size sets how many passage slots each record holds. These counts are exact for a recipe; they predict what the model practices, not how well it will do.
variants.prompt: A second run uses 9,000 questions with 5 retrieved documents each, and keeps an oracle in 60 percent of them. Each oracle-present record holds one oracle and fills the rest of its slots with distractors. How many distractor slots does the whole run hold?
variants.hint: Count the two kinds of record separately, then add the slots.
variants.explanation: Context size multiplies the record count, so a small change in P or in documents per example moves tens of thousands of practice slots.

mistakes.feedback: That treats every slot as a distractor and forgets the oracle sitting in 5,400 records.
That counts distractors in the oracle-present records only and ignores the records with no oracle.

variants.title: Count what the model practices
variants.context: The P fraction sets how many training questions keep an oracle in their context, and the context size sets how many passage slots each record holds. These counts are exact for a recipe; they predict what the model practices, not how well it will do.
variants.prompt: A team raises the retrieved context from 5 to 8 documents per question across 12,000 records. How many additional passage slots does that create?
variants.hint: The question asks for the increase, not the new total.
variants.explanation: Changing the context size changes what the model practices and what each example costs, so plan the count before committing to an expensive run.

mistakes.feedback: That is the new total number of slots, not the increase.
That is the original total at 5 documents per question.

variants.title: Separate the graded signals
variants.context: One end-to-end score hides whether the retriever missed the oracle or the generator ignored good evidence. Oracle recall, answer correctness, citation correctness, distractor resistance, and missing-evidence behavior are graded separately.
variants.prompt: A report shows one end-to-end accuracy number. Match each separate metric to what it measures.

pairs.label: Oracle recall
pairs.detail: How often answer-bearing evidence appears in the retrieved set

pairs.label: Answer correctness
pairs.detail: Whether the final answer satisfies the question

pairs.label: Citation correctness
pairs.detail: Whether the cited passages actually support the claims

pairs.label: Distractor resistance
pairs.detail: Whether plausible unsupported passages change the answer

pairs.label: Missing-evidence behavior
pairs.detail: Whether the model follows the declared answer, defer, or abstain contract

variants.hint: Ask which component each number can convict.
variants.explanation: Grading the pair separately is what tells you whether to fix the retriever or the generator.

variants.title: Separate the graded signals
variants.context: One end-to-end score hides whether the retriever missed the oracle or the generator ignored good evidence. Oracle recall, answer correctness, citation correctness, distractor resistance, and missing-evidence behavior are graded separately.
variants.prompt: Four failure reports arrive from production. Match each symptom to the metric that isolates it.

pairs.label: The answer is wrong and the oracle never reached the prompt
The answer is right but points at a passage that does not support it
A plausible near neighbor in the context flips the answer
The model answers confidently when nothing supports the question

variants.hint: Each symptom implicates a different stage of the pair.
variants.explanation: A single answer score cannot separate a retrieval miss from a generator that ignored good evidence, so each symptom needs its own measurement.

variants.title: Separate the graded signals
variants.context: One end-to-end score hides whether the retriever missed the oracle or the generator ignored good evidence. Oracle recall, answer correctness, citation correctness, distractor resistance, and missing-evidence behavior are graded separately.
variants.prompt: A new engineer mixes up the four terms in the recipe. Match each term to its definition.

pairs.label: Oracle document
pairs.detail: A passage from which the target answer can be supported

pairs.label: Distractor document
pairs.detail: A retrieved passage that does not support the answer

pairs.label: P fraction
pairs.detail: The share of training questions whose context retains an oracle

pairs.label: Evidence target
pairs.detail: An answer that shows which text supports the claim

variants.hint: Two terms describe passages, two describe the recipe.
variants.explanation: The four terms define the recipe: what counts as evidence, what counts as noise, how often evidence is present, and what the answer must demonstrate.

variants.title: Choose the adaptation path
variants.context: Standard RAG refreshes fastest because facts stay in the corpus and it is the first baseline. RAFT fits a bounded domain whose retrieval distribution can be reproduced and whose measured weakness is evidence selection. Domain fine-tuning without documents changes task behavior and format rather than source-grounded knowledge.
variants.prompt: A product catalog is bounded and rarely changes, retrieval can be reproduced exactly, and evaluation shows the generator cites plausible but wrong clauses. What fits?
options: Keep standard RAG and add a prompt instruction telling the model to read carefully.
Fine-tune on the catalog without documents so the model memorizes the clauses.
Build RAFT records with hard distractors from this retriever and fine-tune the generator.
optionFeedback: A prompt instruction does not train evidence selection against the distractors this retriever returns.
Memorized clauses lose attribution and go stale, and the failure was selection rather than knowledge.
Evidence selection is the measured weakness, the domain is bounded, and the retrieval distribution can be reproduced.
variants.hint: What exactly is failing, and can its conditions be reproduced?
variants.explanation: Choose RAFT when the domain is bounded, the production retrieval distribution is reproducible, and evidence selection is the measured generator weakness.

variants.title: Choose the adaptation path
variants.context: Standard RAG refreshes fastest because facts stay in the corpus and it is the first baseline. RAFT fits a bounded domain whose retrieval distribution can be reproduced and whose measured weakness is evidence selection. Domain fine-tuning without documents changes task behavior and format rather than source-grounded knowledge.
variants.prompt: An assistant must always answer in one strict structured format for a stable task, and every fact it needs arrives inside the request itself. What fits?
options: Domain supervised fine-tuning without documents, because the goal is task behavior and format.
RAFT, so the model also practices selecting evidence from retrieved passages.
Standard RAG over a corpus the task does not actually need to consult.
optionFeedback: Supervised fine-tuning without retrieval targets stable task behavior and gives the simplest inference path.
RAFT trains evidence use against retrieved documents, which this task never receives.
Retrieval adds a component with nothing to retrieve and new failure modes to operate.
variants.hint: Is the goal knowledge, or behavior?
variants.explanation: Use domain fine-tuning without documents when the goal is stable task behavior or format rather than source-grounded, updatable knowledge.

variants.title: Choose the adaptation path
variants.context: Standard RAG refreshes fastest because facts stay in the corpus and it is the first baseline. RAFT fits a bounded domain whose retrieval distribution can be reproduced and whose measured weakness is evidence selection. Domain fine-tuning without documents changes task behavior and format rather than source-grounded knowledge.
variants.prompt: An internal wiki is edited daily by dozens of teams and the assistant must reflect an edit within an hour. What fits?
options: Keep standard RAG so facts refresh with the corpus rather than with a checkpoint.
Run RAFT and retrain nightly so the fine-tuned model keeps up with the edits.
Fine-tune on the wiki so the assistant no longer depends on retrieval at all.
optionFeedback: Standard RAG gives the fastest content refresh because the facts remain in the corpus.
A nightly training loop cannot meet an hourly refresh and adds a release gate to every edit.
Baking daily-changing facts into weights makes them stale and hard to attribute.
variants.hint: How fast does each option let a fact change?
variants.explanation: When knowledge changes frequently, keep it in the corpus; fine-tuning is for behavior that should stay stable between releases.
